proposition.claim:
The model is a uniform rooted triangulation \(T_{2n,g_n}\) of an oriented surface, with \(2n\) faces, loops and multiple edges allowed, and \(g_n/n\to\theta\in(0,1/2)\) [Retained latex: \cite[pp.~2--4]{paper}]. Tentacles arise by recursive insertions into a digon; the core is obtained by removing maximal tentacles [Retained latex: \cite[pp.~16--17]{paper}]. Write \(T_n=an\) and \(M_n=2bn\) for their number and total number of internal faces. Lemma 13 supplies positive lower bounds for \(a,b\) with high probability. The deterministic bounds \(a\leq3\), \(b\leq1\) suffice below, since the original map has \(3n\) edges and \(2n\) faces.

Equation reference: eq:pq. Conditionally on these counts and the core, Lemma 14 uses a walk of length \(L=(a+3b)n\). The independent comparison walk \(W\) has increments \(+2,-1\) with respective probabilities \[
p=\frac b{a+3b},\qquad q=\frac{a+2b}{a+3b}.\] Every admissible positive \(a,b\) satisfies \(p+q=1\) and \(0<p<q<1\). Count integrality is inherited from the conditioning; the analytic argument does not posit a nonintegral triangulation. The conditioned walk \(V\) is obtained by an event with probability \(\Omega(n^{-1/2})\), according to the endpoint estimate and cycle-lemma calculation on page 18.

Equation reference: eq:u. For odd \(\ell\), the prescribed word \(w_\ell\) contains \(\ell-1\) up-steps and \(2\ell-1\) down-steps. Its length and probability are therefore \[
|w_\ell|=3\ell-2,\qquad u_\ell=p^{\ell-1}q^{2\ell-1}.\] These are the source’s pattern and hypotheses.

Equation reference: eq:required, eq:ratio. Disjoint blocks give the valid estimate \[\mathbb P(W\hbox{ avoids }w_\ell)\leq(1-u_\ell)^{N_\ell},
\qquad N_\ell=\left\lfloor\frac{(a+3b)n}{3\ell-2}\right\rfloor.\] The source then claims that this last expression is at most \(\exp\{-c'nq^{3\ell}/\ell\}\). Taking negative logarithms would require \[
\frac{N_\ell[-\log(1-u_\ell)]}{(n/\ell)q^{3\ell}}\geq c'.\] For fixed admissible positive \(a,b\) and odd \(\ell\to\infty\) with \(\ell=o(n)\), the left-hand side tends to zero: \[
\frac{u_\ell}{q^{3\ell}}
=\frac1{pq}\left(\frac pq\right)^\ell\longrightarrow0,\quad
\frac{\ell N_\ell}{n}\longrightarrow\frac{a+3b}{3},\quad
\frac{-\log(1-u_\ell)}{u_\ell}\longrightarrow1.\] No fixed positive \(c'\) repairs this inequality with the printed base. Uniformly on the positive lower-count event, \(p/q\leq1/2\) and \(1/(pq)\) is bounded, so the same contradiction holds when \(a,b\) vary with \(n\). The contradiction is algebraic throughout the positive parameter domain, not a finite simulation or a selected unusual triangulation.

The claimed condition on \(s_\theta\) is also insufficient. Because \(pq^2<q^3\), there exist \[\frac1{\log(1/(pq^2))}<s<\frac1{3\log(1/q)}.\] For odd \(\ell=s\log n+O(1)\), a union bound over all starting positions gives \[\mathbb P(W\hbox{ contains }w_\ell)\leq Lu_\ell
=O\!\left(n^{1-s\log(1/(pq^2))}\right)\longrightarrow0.\] Avoidance thus tends to one for this independent walk, whereas the claimed upper bound tends to zero. This refutes the intermediate estimate, not the existence assertion of Lemma 14.

0<theta<1/2; genus g_n/n -> theta. T_n=a n, M_n=2 b n; positive a,b bounded away from zero on Lemma13 event. p=b/(a+3b), q=(a+2b)/(a+3b), 0<p<q<1. ell odd, ell tends to infinity with ell=o(n), including ell=s log n+O(1). word has ell-1 up steps and 2ell-1 down steps.
